title: Sell Mineral Rights in Fontenelle, WY
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights near Fontenelle, WY | Lincoln Co
metaDescription: Own minerals near Fontenelle Reservoir or the Green River corridor in Lincoln County, WY? Get a fair, no-obligation cash offer for your interest.
heroLead: Fontenelle sits along the Green River below the reservoir, closer to the Moxa Arch trend than the Star Valley communities to the west.
intro: That geography matters. The Moxa Arch is a real gas-producing structure that runs through parts of Lincoln and Sweetwater counties, and acreage near Fontenelle has a better chance of sitting inside or near an active or historical unit than land further into Star Valley.

sections.heading: The Moxa Arch connection
paragraphs: Gas production along the Moxa Arch trend has come and gone with commodity prices for decades, mostly tight-sand gas out of the Frontier and Dakota formations. If your minerals sit near the reservoir or along the river corridor, check whether a legacy lease or unit still touches your tract before assuming it's dead ground.

sections.heading: Reservoir and federal land complications
paragraphs: Fontenelle Reservoir itself is a Bureau of Reclamation project, and a fair amount of surrounding land is federally managed. That doesn't erase private mineral ownership nearby, but it does mean more of the map around you is BLM-administered than in Star Valley proper, which shapes how any future unit would be assembled.

sections.heading: What to bring to the table
paragraphs: Your deed, legal description, and any lease history, even expired paperwork, tell a buyer whether your tract has been in play before. If you're holding a royalty interest tied to older Moxa Arch production, recent check stubs make for a faster, more accurate offer.

sections.heading: Reservoir-era leasing records worth checking
paragraphs: Fontenelle Reservoir's construction in the 1960s brought federal survey and land-use activity to this stretch of the Green River, and some of that era's paperwork touches on mineral ownership near the project. If your family's land predates the reservoir, it's worth checking whether any easement or reservation from that period affects your tract.

faqs.question: Is my Fontenelle interest near active gas production?
faqs.answer: It's possible, given the Moxa Arch trend runs through this part of Lincoln County. Pull your legal description and check with the county clerk for any lease or unit of record.

faqs.question: Does nearby BLM land affect my private minerals?
faqs.answer: No, your privately owned mineral interest stays yours regardless of surrounding federal surface or mineral ownership, though it can affect how units get drawn up.

faqs.question: What if my interest has never been leased?
faqs.answer: It can still be sold, priced as speculative acreage rather than producing minerals, based on proximity to the Moxa Arch trend.

faqs.question: Does the reservoir project affect my private mineral ownership?
faqs.answer: Generally no, unless your specific tract was directly involved in the reservoir's construction or right-of-way. Most surrounding private mineral rights were unaffected.
